name: Joe Rogan
role: American podcaster (The Joe Rogan Experience), comedian and UFC commentator
summary: Podcast host who describes himself as not a Republican, pro-choice and a 'bleeding heart liberal' on many issues while backing the Second Amendment, the police and voter ID. He backs publicly funded health care, same-sex marriage, marijuana legalization, a higher minimum wage and a social safety net, but rejects the climate emergency framing, open borders and socialism, and distrusts government and speech restrictions. He has endorsed candidates across the spectrum (Ron Paul, Bernie Sanders in 2020, Donald Trump in 2024) and has criticized Trump on immigration enforcement and foreign wars.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Said in March 2025 that health care 'should be 100 percent socially funded', told Sanders in June 2025 that a community should protect its most vulnerable and most people would accept a national health care system, and repeated it in 2026.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Told Sanders (June 2025) the minimum wage is 'ridiculous' and 'insane' at $7, and rejected the argument that such jobs are only for kids; did not name a target figure.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: On #2501 (about 16:56) Rogan called the idea that billionaires are the problem because they do not pay their fair share 'so weird', and (about 39:57) asked how anyone could propose something as 'insane' as California's wealth tax. On #2341 (about 35:14) he called Sanders's 90 percent top rate 'kind of crazy', though he also said he would pay more if government worked better.

unions-good.rationale: On #2341 (about 56:26) Rogan said unions were created to stop workers being exploited, but that they then become exploited themselves, grow rich and influential, and that this contributed to jobs moving to Mexico. Points both ways.

property-fundamental.rationale: In July 2026 objected to proposals to freeze rents and confiscate bad landlords' property, calling it step one of communist dictatorships.

regulate-corporations.rationale: On #2341 (about 1:08:50) Rogan said Robert Kennedy Jr.'s push to remove synthetic dyes and similar additives from foods is 'very valuable', and agreed that food companies poison children for profit. Limited to food rules.

cut-welfare.rationale: On #2341 (about 1:12:06) Rogan said he is a big supporter of social safety nets, that his family had been on welfare and food stamps and worked its way out, and that without such help people go hungry. He voiced concern about purpose, not about welfare causing dependency.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Said in March 2026 that marijuana 'should be legal', that it is a personal freedom issue and 'leave people alone'; also says psychedelics like MDMA and ibogaine should be accessible. Separates these from heroin and opiates, so full legalization of all drugs is not stated.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Said you 'should be able to talk about anything' (Dec 2025), argued banning online 'crazy talk' protects the dumbest members of society, and criticized UK speech arrests (Feb 2026).

limit-guns.rationale: Said he believes in the Second Amendment (2022) and Wikipedia lists gun rights among his stated positions; no quote opposing limits on all ownership, so not -2.

empower-police-military.rationale: Said in Oct 2024 'what you should do is fund the police', with better training; in 2022 said he supports the military and police. Did not address expanding police authority.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Called opposition to gay marriage homophobic and a reason he is not a Republican (2022).

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes himself as 'pro choice' (Sept 2024); objected to forcing a child to carry a rapist's baby (2022) and to Texas going after women who travel (2025); has voiced discomfort about later-stage fetuses.

more-religion-public.rationale: On #2526 (about 47:52 to 50:20) Rogan sided with the view that mandating the Ten Commandments in schools would push people away from Christianity and described its backers as wealthy Christian nationalists; he did not say religion has no public role.

reduce-immigration.rationale: On #2437 (about 2:16:33 to 2:25:40) Rogan criticized the open border and non-citizen counting in the census, but also called the shooting of a woman by an ICE officer in Minnesota 'all kinds of wrong' and questioned deporting people who have lived in the country most of their lives. He did not say how many legal immigrants should be admitted.

free-trade.rationale: Said in Sept 2024 that moving manufacturing to third-world countries to save corporations money 'did not do this country any justice'.

open-borders.rationale: Said 'you can't have an open border' because criminals and cartel members would come through (Feb 2026), and called the open border under Biden 'insane' (2026).

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In June 2025 called the 'climate change emergency' a vehicle for money and control, objected to carbon footprint tracking and carbon taxes, and questioned the warming narrative, while agreeing pollution is bad.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Told Trump (Oct 2024) that nuclear is probably the cleanest, safest electricity and that fears rest on a few old disasters; also called coal-powered electric cars ridiculous.

central-planning.rationale: In July 2026 said socialism and communism 'always lead' to a powerful military government that controls the population.

basic-income.rationale: Mixed within 2025: in June said of UBI 'I support it' as an answer to automation, but worried it breeds dependence and state control; in Sept 2025 said you can't just give people free money. Recorded as ambivalent, not as opposed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In 2025 Rogan called the friction with Canada over tariffs stupid, yet in another segment he recounted Ross Perot's tariff and jobs argument approvingly and said he voted for him. Mixed.

separate-church-state.rationale: On #2352 (about 9:53) Rogan agreed that the separation of church and state has always been very important and that imposing religion on children in non-religious schools 'seems kind of crazy'; on #2526 (about 47:52) he repeated Talarico's argument and said putting the Ten Commandments in schools is not the right way to do it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Said in Jan 2026 'I don't think you should impose any kind of religion on any people'; fears of theocracy are understandable.

harm-principle.rationale: In March 2026 said 'stop coming up with laws where you can impose your values and your morals' on other people and let them make personal choices, 'and that should apply to a lot of things'.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: In July 2026 called it 'crazy' that migrants who crossed the border were put on Medicaid and Social Security and given hotels and phones; said he also thinks long-term residents deserve some amnesty.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Called government 'incompetent, corrupt' (2025), said the political system turns people into sociopaths (2026), and agreed US campaign finance is corrupt.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Said in July 2026 that mandating the Ten Commandments in classrooms promotes Christianity and that promoting religion belongs to churches while public schools should be educational; teaching about religion is fine.

separated-powers.rationale: On #2341 (about 1:39:05) Rogan called the Founders' system of checks and balances incredible and praised their grasp of human desire for power and corruption.

priority-to-poor.rationale: On #2341 (about 23:57) Rogan said that viewing the country as a community, the most important thing is to protect its most vulnerable members. A close statement of the principle, not about laws specifically.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Hunter who promotes 'Eat What You Kill' as an alternative to factory farming and mistreatment of animals.

corporate-influence.rationale: Agreed with Sanders (2025) that the campaign finance system is corrupt, and in 2026 said the revolving door from regulator to industry is a loophole that should be closed.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: In his 2024 Netflix special, as quoted by Wikipedia, Rogan said he believes in trans people and supports an adult's right to do whatever makes them happy, but that society needs standards and a trans woman should not simply use the women's room. He has also said trans women should not compete in women's sports. Mixed.

assisted-dying.rationale: On #2470 (about 11:36 to 13:09) Rogan said that for a terminally ill person, like his friend Michael Lair who went to Oregon with ALS and wanted to die on his own terms, 'there's a place for it', while objecting to its use for mental illness or seasonal depression in Canada.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Called defunding police 'stupid' and said police are necessary (2024, 2026). Prisons not addressed, so medium.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Said in June 2025 'I'm a big supporter of social safety nets' (his family was on welfare) and likened them to the fire department that everyone pays into.

rent-control.rationale: In July 2026 criticized New York mayoral proposals to freeze rents as step one toward confiscation.

free-public-college.rationale: Said in June 2025 that 'we all believe there should be free public education' and that the university system should also be funded because it would benefit everyone; in 2019 called free education 'a wonderful thing'.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Objected in June 2025 to a carbon tax on ordinary people as a way to 'extract more money' from them; did not address taxing polluters generally.

voter-id.rationale: Said in Oct 2024 that arguments against voter ID are 'ridiculous', and in July 2026 that he sees no reason for having none and that it is not racist to require it.

notes:
Talk-show conversations mix his views with guests' and jokes; only statements he clearly made as his own were used. Views changed over time: 2019-20 support for UBI gave way to a 2025 statement against 'free money'; Sanders (2020) to Trump (2024), later criticized Trump on ICE raids, Iran and Epstein. Positions on trans athletes, immigration, Israel, Ukraine, free speech and COVID mandates exist but do not map cleanly to any current statement, so those statements are null. No on-camera political quiz was found. Transcripts of 2024-2026 episodes (Singju Post, speaker-labelled; PodScripts, unlabelled) supplied most answers; only lines labelled as Rogan, or clearly his in context, were used. Rogan often voices guests' framing, so views he only relayed or asked about were skipped.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 12 answers taken from it, 18 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Based on unofficial auto-generated transcripts and captions that do not label speakers; only passages where Rogan is clearly the speaker (replying directly to a named guest, addressing his producer, or quoted by a commentator) were used. His views have shifted over time (Sanders in 2020, Trump in 2024, criticism of some Trump actions in 2025-26); the most recent clear position is used. Several of his best-known topics (COVID mandates, Ukraine, Israel, trans athletes) were discussed at length but match no statement in the list or could not be attributed reliably. YouTube access was blocked partway through the run, so the Netflix special was not read directly.
